title: Bretton AI announces strategic alliance with Kroll to bring AI agents to the hardest parts of compliance
summary: Bretton AI and Kroll form a strategic alliance to bring AI agents into KYC, AML, and sanctions investigations, with every step documented for examiners.
body_markdown:
*The alliance pairs Kroll’s financial crime advisory expertise with Bretton AI’s agents, helping institutions apply AI where it has the most impact, with governance in place from the start.*


Every financial institution is asking where AI can make the biggest difference in compliance. Bretton AI and[Kroll](https://www.kroll.com/en/services/investigations-diligence-and-compliance/ai-enabled-financial-crime-compliance-services) have formed a strategic alliance to help banks, credit unions, and fintechs answer that question and put AI to work where it counts.


The question is getting harder to put off. Alert volumes are climbing, regulatory expectations are rising, and much of the investigative work behind compliance remains manual. Adopting AI in a regulated environment also means deciding which workflows to automate, how to govern them, and how to document the results for examiners.


The alliance covers both sides of that decision. Kroll contributes the judgment of an advisor institutions have relied on for nearly a century. Bretton AI provides agents that carry out KYC, AML, and sanctions investigations, with every step documented and ready for review.


## Kroll knows where compliance programs break


Kroll is a global financial and risk advisory firm that has spent decades building and stress-testing compliance programs. Today, Kroll's 6,500 experts across more than 30 countries and territories worldwide include former regulators, prosecutors, compliance leaders, and investigators. Their work spans financial crime compliance, regulatory remediation, independent monitorships, and complex investigations.


Kroll's financial crime teams work alongside compliance teams day to day, so they see firsthand where analyst time goes.


Across the institutions Kroll advises, the same pressure points emerge consistently. Alert queues grow faster than teams can clear them, and most alerts turn out to be false positives. Much of each analyst's time goes to due diligence and to writing up each case. Teams know what thorough, defensible work requires. What they lack is time.


The strain is sharpest at correspondent banks, where many counterparties have no KYC file and analysts research them from public sources.


## Bretton AI agents take on the work behind each pressure point


Bretton AI’s agents take on that preparation. They connect to the case management, screening, and core systems an institution already runs and follow its own procedures. Each case comes back to an analyst to review and decide. Here is what the agents handle in the three areas where teams feel the most strain:


- **KYC and EDD reviews.** Agents gather customer records, review documentation, and run open-source and adverse media research. Analysts receive a complete case file for sign-off.
- **AML alerts and transaction monitoring investigations.** Agents triage each alert, analyze account and counterparty activity, and escalate matters that need a risk-based decision, with a fully cited narrative.
- **Sanctions alert reviews.** Agents evaluate each potential match against sanctions, politically exposed person (PEP), and adverse media lists, then present a documented recommendation. Analysts confirm true matches and clear the rest with the evidence in front of them.


Institutions using Bretton have reduced EDD case handling times by more than 80 percent, and some have cut transaction monitoring triage from more than 30 minutes to under five. Analysts still make the call on every case. What changes is how much of their day goes to preparing it.


## How Bretton AI and Kroll work together


Bringing AI into a compliance program is a governance decision as well as a technology one. The alliance gives institutions support on both.


On governance, Kroll brings the perspective of an advisor that has spent decades inside financial crime programs. Its team helps institutions decide where AI belongs, how to oversee it, and how it fits with the systems and controls already in place.


On technology, Bretton AI brings agents built for regulated work. Each agent follows the institution’s own procedures and runs on top of its existing systems. Before it goes live, it is tested against the institution’s past investigations through[a structured path to production](https://www.bretton.com/blog/from-onsite-to-production-how-bretton-ai-takes-an-agent-live) .


With both firms involved, institutions get clear guidance on where to start and agents ready to put it into practice. Throughout, the institution stays in control. It owns its agents, and its compliance team keeps ownership of policy, risk assessments, and final outcomes.


> *“Financial institutions need to understand where AI can make a practical difference and what it takes to use it responsibly. Kroll brings the investigative and regulatory experience to help clients make those decisions and guide implementation. Our strategic alliance with Bretton AI builds on that expertise, helping institutions increase investigative capacity while keeping human judgment, governance and accountability central.”*


Tom Bock, Managing Director, Head of U.S. Financial Crime Advisory Practice, Kroll


## Every agent step is documented for examiners


When an examiner asks how an alert was worked, the institution can show every source the agent consulted and each step it took to reach its recommendation. Bretton AI records each recommendation with its reasoning and evidence. Its Trust Infrastructure adds model risk management controls, continuous evaluation, and quality assurance testing across every agent.


> *“In financial crime compliance, a decision is only as defensible as the evidence behind it. Bretton’s agents document every recommendation source by source, with the same rigor Kroll has brought to its own work for decades. That common ground is what our alliance is built on.”*


Will Lawrence, Co-Founder & CEO, Bretton AI


## The next step for compliance teams


For most financial institutions, the open question is where to begin with AI in compliance, and how to do it with the right governance and oversight. The strategic alliance pairs technology built for regulated environments with advisors who know those environments deeply.


Together, Bretton AI and Kroll help institutions start with the reviews that place the greatest strain on their teams, so experienced analysts can focus on the cases that warrant their expertise.
